concept: Marinade mSOL and Sanctum INF and bSOL and JupSOL
summary: Source-anchored research for Marinade mSOL and Sanctum INF and bSOL and JupSOL. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: INF is a reward-bearing (not rebasing) token for Sanctum's Infinity pool, a basket of LSTs. Its yield is the weighted average staking yield of the LSTs held plus swap fees earned by routing trades between them. (medium confidence)

Marinade allocates stake through the Stake Auction Marketplace (SAM), where validators bid for stake. Critics said winning bids implied APY above on-chain native yield (over 10% before the period reported) and that unverified Discord claims put 2.7M SOL with sybil or sandwiching validators. Marinade answered that SAM is not an active policy maker and that no objective methodology exists to identify malicious validators. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2025-01-31)

bSOL is BlazeStake's liquid staking token. The pool account is owned by the official SPL stake pool program from Solana Labs. BlazeStake's docs say it pioneered Custom Liquid Staking, which lets a user direct stake to chosen validators. It sets each validator's stake from a coefficient based on APY, performance and decentralization, leaves out the roughly 32 validators of the superminority, and keeps 0.05% of stake in reserve for instant unstake. The docs say the program was audited seven times by five firms and that its upgrade authority is an ecosystem multisig overseen by the Solana Foundation. (high confidence)

Neodyme warns that Infinity carries 'significant indirect smart contract risk': a bug in the fund tracking or token minting of any LST protocol it prices could put all of Infinity's liquidity at risk, because each SOL value calculator mirrors that protocol's own accounting. At audit time the admin authority could add LSTs and set calculators, so a malicious calculator could drain the pool. Sanctum then planned a hot-wallet admin during setup and a team multisig for upgrades. The S Controller can pause all pool operations. The current authority setup was not checked. (medium confidence)

SAM bond rules: a funded Protected Staking Rewards (PSR) bond is required, and settlement charges it each epoch for the previous epoch's stake. Target coverage is 13 epochs. If the bond covers fewer than 5 epochs of expected revenue, the Bond Risk Reduction Mechanism undelegates enough stake that the remaining bond covers the remaining stake for 13 epochs, and charges a fee proportional to the undelegated amount from the bond. A Bid Reduction Penalty applies if a validator's bid falls below its effective bid of the previous 3 epochs. An Activating Stake Fee charges validators for newly activating stake, scaled by how far the bid is above the clearing rate. MIP-19 proposed the risk-reduction mechanism and the activation payment. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-04)

Sanctum-operated stake pools such as JupSOL run the SanctumSplMulti deployment of the SPL Stake Pool Program, which Jupiter docs say has been audited nine times. Sanctum handles day-to-day management, and its fee changes are capped and need advance notice. (low confidence)

Across SPL stake pool LSTs, the staker authority can redelegate stake and raise fees (fee increases are capped and take at least one epoch to apply), and the pool program is upgraded by a multisig. Jupiter docs say JupSOL's upgrade authority is an 11-member multisig with a threshold of 6. (medium confidence)

mSOL, JupSOL, INF and bSOL are all reward-bearing tokens, not rebasing tokens. A holder's token count stays fixed and each token redeems for more SOL as rewards accrue. Marinade prices mSOL as total staked SOL divided by mSOL minted. Jupiter says the JupSOL/SOL ratio rises over time. Sanctum calls INF reward-bearing, not rebasing. BlazeStake says bSOL is designed to rise against SOL every epoch. (high confidence)

At the end of each epoch Infinity compares its SOL reserve with a target. If the reserve is above target, it stakes the excess into Sanctum's top-performing LSTs inside the pool. If the reserve is below target, it unstakes the worst-performing LSTs to refill the reserve. Sanctum's technical docs are the only source for this rule, and the docs are undated. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

The four tokens run on different on-chain code. mSOL is issued by Marinade's own Anchor/Rust liquid-staking program (repo marinade-finance/liquid-staking-program, which also holds the mSOL-to-SOL swap pool). bSOL uses the official Solana Labs SPL stake-pool program, and BlazeStake states that other major pools use third-party contracts. JupSOL and other Sanctum LSTs use Sanctum's fork of the SPL stake pool program, pinned to the program@v1.0.0 tag (Jupiter calls the JupSOL deployment SanctumSplMulti). INF is the LP token of Sanctum's Infinity pool, run by the S Controller program with a separate Pricing Program. (high confidence)
